recent_posts.title: Distributed Python dataframes and machine learning with Livebook and Elixir
recent_posts.summary: Livebook, Elixir's computational notebook platform, now features full Python integration funded by NGI0 Commons Fund. Key additions include reproducible Python environments via uv, Python cells with autocompletion and documentation on hover, zero-copy Apache Arrow data transfers between Elixir and Python, distributed Python execution using Erlang's distribution model with a distributed garbage collector, and support for spawning Python/Elixir workloads across Kubernetes and Fly.io clusters via FLAME integration. Developers can load data in Elixir and manipulate it with Polars or Pandas in Python, pass remote object references without copying, and scale workflows using Elixir's fault-tolerance primitives.

recent_posts.title: Type systems are leaky abstractions: the case of Map.take!/2
recent_posts.summary: José Valim explores the limitations of type systems through the lens of a proposed Map.take!/2 function in Elixir. The function takes a map and a list of keys, returning only those keys while raising if any are missing. While trivial to implement in a dynamic language, typing it precisely proves difficult: a broad map() return type loses all key information, and TypeScript's keyof/Pick approach breaks down when keys are computed conditionally rather than inlined. Refactoring the inline calls into a variable causes TypeScript to widen the type to string[], losing precision. Using 'as const' restores some precision but introduces unsoundness — the type claims keys may be present that aren't guaranteed at runtime. The only sound alternative returns Partial types, defeating the function's purpose. Macros are proposed as an escape hatch: by requiring the key list to be a compile-time literal, the macro can expand to precise record access expressions the type system can verify. The post concludes that dynamic programs can be correct yet unverifiable by type systems, and that adding types to dynamic languages involves real trade-offs between expressiveness, boilerplate, and type system complexity.

recent_posts.title: Why Elixir achieves the highest LLM completion rates
recent_posts.summary: A Tencent study found Elixir achieved the highest LLM completion rate (97.5%) among 20 programming languages. The language's immutability enables clear local reasoning without side effects, explicit documentation with testable examples creates high-quality training data, and decade-long stability means no conflicting information across versions. Beyond single-pass generation, Elixir's fast parallel compilation, detailed warnings, low operational complexity (no need for Redis/RabbitMQ/Lambda), and runtime introspection make it well-suited for iterative coding agent workflows.

recent_posts.title: Zero Trust Auth for Plug/Phoenix apps is here
recent_posts.summary: Dashbit released nimble_zta, a library enabling Zero Trust Authentication for Plug/Phoenix applications. The library integrates with cloud providers (CloudFlare, GCP, Tailscale) to handle identity and access control, allowing applications in private clouds to leverage existing organizational authentication systems without custom integration. Extracted from Livebook, it joins Dashbit's collection of focused "nimble" libraries for the Elixir ecosystem.

recent_posts.title: The path to Tidewave: beyond code intelligence
recent_posts.summary: Tidewave.ai introduces runtime intelligence for AI development tools by connecting editors and AI assistants directly to language runtimes, providing access to logs, databases, and REPLs. Unlike static code analysis tools, Tidewave runs as an MCP server within web applications to understand both code structure and runtime behavior. The vision extends beyond code intelligence to comprehend the actual value delivered by applications, focusing on AI augmentation rather than developer replacement while maintaining the advantages of local development environments.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Tidewave: beyond code intelligence
recent_posts.summary: Tidewave is a new collection of AI development tools that goes beyond static code analysis by providing runtime intelligence. It connects AI assistants to running applications through MCP servers, giving them access to logs, databases, REPLs, and live system state. The platform aims to enhance developer productivity by understanding not just code structure but how applications actually run and deliver value to users. Currently supporting Phoenix and Rails frameworks, Tidewave focuses on augmenting rather than replacing developers, helping them reach their productivity zones across different skill areas.

recent_posts.title: Embedding Python in Elixir, it's Fine
recent_posts.summary: Elixir's Nx ecosystem is growing, with projects like Pythonx enabling seamless integration of Python's capabilities within Elixir. Pythonx embeds the Python interpreter in the Erlang VM, allowing for automatic data conversion and code evaluation. This new tool simplifies the inclusion of Python workflows in Elixir, enhancing machine learning and data processing. Additionally, Livebook's support for both languages streamlines computational tasks, making Elixir a versatile choice for data-centric applications.

recent_posts.title: Dashbit plans for 2025
recent_posts.summary: Dashbit is expanding its subscription team to four engineers, including prominent members like José Valim. They aim to reduce waiting times for their Elixir Development Subscription service and increase contributions to open source projects. Plans for 2025 include enhancements to Elixir’s type system, the release of Phoenix v1.8, and new projects like ElixirKit and NimbleZTA. Additionally, tools such as Livebook Teams and improved interoperability with other languages are on the horizon.

recent_posts.title: Data evolution with set-theoretic types
recent_posts.summary: This post explores how set-theoretic types in Elixir can address issues with data evolution in statically typed languages, focusing on maintaining backwards compatibility in library data definitions. It discusses challenges with breaking changes, illustrates the use of structural subtyping, explains a proposed versioning mechanism called revisions, and emphasizes the importance of type safety and progressive data evolution.

recent_posts.title: Remix's concurrent submissions are fundamentally flawed (without causal ordering)
recent_posts.summary: The author critiques the trade-offs and flaws in Remix's approach to concurrent submissions and revalidation, highlighting issues such as race conditions, lag due to double round-trips, and incorrect assumptions about data versioning. Alternative solutions involving causal ordering and persistent connections, like those used in Phoenix LiveView, are discussed to address these flaws and improve user experience.

top_posts.title: Elixir and Machine Learning: Nx v0.1 released!
top_posts.summary: Numerical Elixir is a language for numerical computing and machine learning. Nx is a library that brings multi-dimensional arrays (tensors) and just-in-time compilation of numerical Elixir to both CPU and GPU. In this blog post, we will discuss the current state of Nx, some of its upcoming features and take a look at its growing ecosystem.

top_posts.title: Soft deletes with Ecto and PostgreSQL
top_posts.summary: Learn how to implement soft deletions in Ecto and PostgreSQL using rules and views. The post discusses adding a `deleted_at` column, creating PostgreSQL rules to convert deletes into updates, and using views to filter out deleted records. It also addresses handling stale records and provides a method for effectively deleting data when necessary. Various caveats and alternatives, like using triggers, are also covered.

top_posts.title: Announcing Phoenix Playground
top_posts.summary: Announcing Phoenix Playground, the easiest way to run single-file Phoenix applications. It provides all the basic pieces needed for a Phoenix app, supports live code reloading, and has built-in testing capabilities.

top_posts.title: Supercharge your app: latency and rendering optimizations in Phoenix LiveView
top_posts.summary: LiveView is a library for the Phoenix web framework that allows you to write rich, real-time user experiences with server-rendered HTML. It has undergone several optimizations, such as splitting statics from dynamics, rendering trees and fingerprints, change tracking, LiveComponents, tree-sharing in LiveComponents, and change-tracking revisited.

top_posts.title: SDKs with Req: S3
top_posts.summary: The post discusses implementing a minimalistic custom SDK for AWS S3 instead of using large, feature-rich packages. It covers essential tasks such as putting and getting objects in a bucket, discusses S3 API ubiquity across various storage services, and introduces ReqS3, a plugin for handling S3 tasks with custom authentication, XML parsing, and pre-signed URLs. The post advocates starting with a minimal implementation and scaling complexity only as needed.
